questions.stem: The piece of apparatus used to deliver one fixed, accurate volume of solution into the conical flask during a titration is the

options.text: burette
pipette
measuring cylinder
volumetric flask

questions.explanation: A pipette is calibrated to deliver a single fixed volume, typically 20.0 or 25.0 cm3, with high accuracy. The burette by contrast delivers whatever variable volume is needed to reach the end point, and that volume is the titre.

distractorRationale.a: A burette delivers a variable volume read from a scale, not a single fixed one
distractorRationale.c: A measuring cylinder is far too imprecise for quantitative analysis
distractorRationale.d: A volumetric flask is used to prepare a standard solution, not to deliver one

questions.stem: 25.0 cm3 of potassium hydroxide solution was exactly neutralised by 20.0 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid. What is the concentration of the potassium hydroxide?

options.text: 0.125 mol/dm3
0.200 mol/dm3

questions.explanation: HCl + KOH -> KCl + H2O has a 1 : 1 ratio. Moles of acid = 0.100 x 0.0200 = 0.00200 mol, so moles of KOH are also 0.00200. Concentration = 0.00200 / 0.0250 = 0.0800 mol/dm3. Since less acid than base was needed, the base must be the more dilute of the two, which it is.

distractorRationale.a: The volumes were used the wrong way round, giving 0.1 x 25 divided by 40
distractorRationale.c: The volume ratio was inverted, dividing 25.0 by 20.0 instead of 20.0 by 25.0
distractorRationale.d: The acid concentration was doubled, as if the acid were dibasic

questions.stem: A student records these titres: rough 25.00 cm3, first 24.20 cm3, second 24.30 cm3, third 24.90 cm3. The correct average titre to use is
questions.explanation: The rough titration is always discarded. Of the remaining three, only 24.20 and 24.30 agree within 0.10 cm3 and so count as concordant; 24.90 is an outlier. The average is (24.20 + 24.30) / 2 = 24.25 cm3.

distractorRationale.b: All three accurate titres were averaged, including the non-concordant 24.90
distractorRationale.c: All four readings including the rough titre were averaged
distractorRationale.d: The rough titre was included instead of the first accurate one

questions.stem: What volume, in cm3, of 0.100 mol/dm3 tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is required to neutralise 25.0 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 sodium hydroxide? H2SO4 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O
questions.explanation: Moles of NaOH = 0.100 x 0.0250 = 0.00250 mol. The ratio of acid to base is 1 : 2, so moles of H2SO4 = 0.00250 / 2 = 0.00125 mol. Volume = 0.00125 / 0.100 = 0.0125 dm3, which is 12.5 cm3. Because the acid is dibasic, only half the volume is needed at equal concentration.

questions.stem: A student rinses the conical flask with the alkali solution instead of with distilled water before pipetting the alkali into it. The effect on the titre will be that it is

options.text: too high, because extra alkali is present and more acid is needed
too low, because the flask is already partly neutralised
unchanged, since the same alkali is involved
unchanged, because rinsing removes all traces of liquid

questions.explanation: The pipette already delivers an exactly known amount of alkali. Any film of alkali left by rinsing adds extra moles that were never accounted for, so more acid must be run in to reach the end point and the titre reads high. Distilled water is safe because it adds no moles, only volume.

distractorRationale.b: Nothing has been neutralised; extra alkali makes the flask contents more, not less, alkaline
distractorRationale.c: The identity of the liquid is not the issue; the extra unmeasured quantity is
distractorRationale.d: Rinsing always leaves a thin film of liquid on the glass, which is exactly why distilled water is specified

questions.stem: Before a titration, the burette should be rinsed with

options.text: distilled water only
the solution it is going to contain
the solution in the conical flask
dilute sodium hydroxide

questions.explanation: Any distilled water clinging to the inside of the burette would dilute the titrant, so a larger volume would be needed and the titre would read too high. Rinsing with the titrant itself means that the film left behind has exactly the intended concentration.

distractorRationale.a: Water left in the burette dilutes the titrant and biases the result
distractorRationale.c: That would introduce the other reactant and cause a reaction inside the burette
distractorRationale.d: Adding an unrelated alkali would react with an acidic titrant and ruin the analysis

questions.stem: In a titration experiment, the endpoint is indicated by a change in color of the indicator. What is this change typically associated with?

options.text: The solution becoming cloudy
A sudden temperature change
A distinct color change
The formation of a precipitate

questions.explanation: The endpoint of a titration is marked by a distinct color change due to the indicator used. This change signifies that the acid has completely reacted with the base, indicating that the titration is complete.

distractorRationale.a: Cloudiness is not a reliable indicator of the endpoint in acid-base titrations.
distractorRationale.b: Temperature changes can occur but are not used as an endpoint indicator.
distractorRationale.d: The formation of a precipitate may occur in some reactions but is not typical for acid-base titrations.
